content.body:
Prior to 1942, the German Fallschirmjager were equipped with only pistols and hand grenades, with heavier equipment being dropped separately. This proved disasterous during the Battle of Crete, where rifle and machine gun fire inflicted heavy casualties on the outgunned paratroopers as they attempted to retrieve weapons that were scattered all over the battlefield. This experience prompted the development of a rifle that could be carried on the paratrooper.
The FG42 was in many ways a weapon ahead of its time, and it would go on to heavily influence post-war firearm design. Since it was intended for paratroopers saving weight was extremely important, and to this end its tolerances are extremly tight: The weapon is really some of Germany's greatest minds making the best weapon they possibly could at the time.
The weapon's biggest drawback is its limited magazine: The heavier ammunition plus the side-mounted magazine meant that carrying much more would unbalance the weapon. The heavy cartridge also give the weapon a lot of muzzle rise, which limited the usefullness of full-auomatic fire. Still, the weapon was very well received and, despite its limited production, it ended up as an iconic weapon of the war.
